name: Cardenas hydrophilic-catheter SCI trial
question: Does a hydrophilic-coated intermittent catheter delay symptomatic urinary tract infection compared with an uncoated catheter after acute traumatic spinal cord injury?

design.blinding: open-label; participants and clinical staff could not be blinded

arms.label: single-use uncoated polyvinyl chloride Conveen catheter

design.population: 224 adults with traumatic spinal cord injury less than three months old, neurogenic bladder dysfunction, and intermittent catheterization at least three times daily were randomized at 15 North American spinal cord injury centers.
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, open-label, parallel-group randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Population and Study Design, p 409; Results, Baseline Characteristics and Participant Flow, p 411

verdictNote: First treated UTI was delayed; full-period UTI incidence did not differ, despite lower institutional incidence.
takeaway: In 224 adults with acute traumatic spinal cord injury, hydrophilic-coated SpeediCath delayed first antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI versus uncoated Conveen in an adjusted analysis of 188 participants (HR 0.666, 95% CI 0.453–0.978); institutional UTI incidence was lower, full-period incidence was not.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Cardenas DD, Moore KN, Dannels-McClure A, et al. "Intermittent Catheterization With a Hydrophilic-Coated Catheter Delays Urinary Tract Infections in Acute Spinal Cord Injury: A Prospective, Randomized, Multicenter Trial." *PM R.* 2011;3(5):408-417. doi:10.1016/j.pmrj.2011.01.001
reports.followUp: During hospitalization or rehabilitation and up to three months after discharge; maximum six months.
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Study Design, p 409

results.endpoint: Time to first antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI
results.measure: Time from first catheterization to first antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI, clinical definition; Cox analysis of participants with complete covariates
results.note: Clinical UTI meant antibiotic treatment prescribed. Of 219 exposed participants, 31 were excluded from the covariate-adjusted analysis because of missing covariates or UTI before first assigned-catheter use; the paper does not give an exact delay duration.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Procedure, p 410; Results, Time to Onset of the First Symptomatic UTI, p 412; Figure 3 caption, p 413

results.endpoint: Antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI incidence during institutional care
results.measure: Clinical-definition UTI episodes per observed patient-month during institutional care
results.note: The paper reports 21% lower clinical-definition incidence and RR 1.40 in the uncoated versus coated direction. For strict-definition UTI, rates were 0.189/month (21/111.3) coated and 0.295/month (42/142.2) uncoated; reported RR 1.67 in the uncoated versus coated direction; P = .022.
results.locator: Full text, Results, UTI Incidence, p 412; Table 2, p 413

results.endpoint: Time to first strict-definition symptomatic UTI
results.measure: Time from first catheterization to first antibiotic-treated UTI also meeting bacteriuria ≥10² CFU/mL, symptom, and leukocyte-esterase criteria
results.note: Strict-definition first-UTI comparison was not statistically significant at the two-sided .05 threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Procedure, p 410; Results, Time to Onset of the First Symptomatic UTI, p 412

results.endpoint: Symptomatic UTI incidence over full study period
results.measure: Clinical- and strict-definition UTI episodes per observed patient-month across institutional and community periods
results.note: No difference in symptomatic UTI incidence was detected over the combined institutional and community follow-up.
results.locator: Full text, Results, UTI Incidence, p 412; Table 2, p 413

harms.label: Urethral bleeding adverse-event reports
harms.note: P < .05; 10 of 14 coated-arm bleeding reports occurred in the first eight days. Event reports are not unique-patient counts.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, Safety Outcomes, p 414

harms.label: Microhematuria on daily dipstick in institutional weeks 3–4
harms.note: Mean 10.0 measurements per participant; P < .0001. Percentages use tests, not participants, as denominators; total test counts are not reported.

delivery.label: Catheter assignment
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Design and Study Materials, pp 409–410
delivery.note: Randomization occurred within ten days of starting intermittent catheterization. Both catheters were sterile and discarded after one use; SpeediCath was ready to use in sterile water-based solution, whereas Conveen required gel from a single-use sachet.

delivery.label: Study completion and premature discontinuation
delivery.value: 114 of 224 randomized participants completed; five stopped before first assigned-catheter use and 105 discontinued prematurely after starting
delivery.note: The paper reports premature discontinuation in 57% of coated users versus 39% of uncoated users; change in bladder management was the main reason (34 coated, 29 uncoated).
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, Baseline Characteristics and Participant Flow, p 411; Discussion, p 415
